chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade drawing the sword in the mosque and sharpening arrows in the mosque.
And he said: 'It was built for other than that.'
ai.seo_question: What martial actions are forbidden inside the mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Alaa ibn al-Harish and Muhammad ibn Muslim, underscores the sanctity of the mosque (masjid) as a space exclusively dedicated to worship and tranquility, distinct from martial activities. In Shia jurisprudence, this prohibition extends beyond mere physical presence of weapons to include the preparatory acts of drawing swords and sharpening arrows, reinforcing the mosque's role as a sanctuary of peace. The Prophet’s clarification that it was 'built for that purpose' highlights the theological intent of the structure, a principle often linked to the concept of 'Taharah' (purity) in ritual and spiritual contexts.
